analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Per the patch, the edits are: the 'Last updated' date bump (line 3), a sentence at ~line 99 saying each provider test shard runs on its own CI lane `test-provider-K` with a link to build.md#ci-runner-routing, and wording at ~lines 1344-1349 saying the runner-routing checks pin per-shard lanes that match the job matrix. These are documentation-only edits. No source, protocol, authentication, attestation, encryption, cache or key-handling code changed. I found no regression against the threat model entries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, T-041 and others), and no new attack surface. The routing text describes CI runner lane selection, which is outside the provider threat model's scope. It mentions the CI plane, but this document does not alter that plane's trust or permissions. The statement that routed jobs keep read-only permissions and fork PRs are handled safely is descriptive, and I could not verify it from the supplied evidence. I did not see the CI workflow files, the runner-routing script or build.md#ci-runner-routing. The security of the real routing (label grants, fork handling) would need review in the workflow changes if any exist in other batches. The test-doc sections I read (add-on hold, endpoint resumption/logout, SSD test working volume, checkpoint storage) are unchanged context. They say tests must use isolated state and never production cache roots or keys, which is consistent with the threat model. No findings.
